mainTopic: The holiness of בכורות in the מדבר, and קונטרוקוס's number questions about the לויים and the double holy מנה
overview: This amud finishes the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about whether the בכורות in the מדבר stayed holy after the לויים replaced them. רבי אלעזר brings רבי יוחנן's source, 'לי יהיו', and the גמרא explains how רבי יוחנן reads ריש לקיש's verse as a reward: this מצוה brings you into the land. רב מרדכי reports a version that sounds reversed but means the same thing, which teaches that one must repeat a teaching in his teacher's exact words. Then קונטרוקוס the officer asks רבן יוחנן בן זכאי two number puzzles. First, why the לויים total 22,000 when their families add up to 22,300. The answer is that the 300 extra were firstborns, who could not free an Israelite firstborn. Second, why about 201 talents of silver were collected for the משכן but only 100 were given. The answer is that the holy מנה was double. The גמרא then searches for a source for the double מנה. Two proofs from how the Torah writes amounts are rejected, and רב חסדא brings a verse in יחזקאל that defines the מנה. The calculation from that verse continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of ריש לקיש's statement: their holiness stopped
steps.stepSummary: The closing word of ריש לקיש's position: the בכורות in the מדבר became holy, and then their holiness stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and then it stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes ריש לקיש's statement on the previous amud. He said the בכורות became holy, and then their holiness stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's full view has three stages. First, the בכורות were holy in Egypt and the מדבר. Next, their holiness stopped after the census, when the לוים took their place. Finally, it came back when the Jews entered ארץ ישראל. The word ופסקו is the middle stage, and it is exactly where רבי יוחנן disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: They stopped, they ceased (here: the holiness of the firstborn stopped)
Firstborn (people or animals) that have special holiness

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the last word of a sentence that began on the previous amud. Read it as the end of ריש לקיש's opinion.

phrases.english: and [then their sanctity] ceased.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפָסְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement of ריש לקיש begun earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, the holiness of the בכורות in the מדבר stopped after the census.

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן's source?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש already has a verse for his view. The גמרא asks what source רבי יוחנן has for saying the holiness never stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for ריש לקיש, because he gave his reason. But for רבי יוחנן, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says ריש לקיש's view is fine because he already explained his source. Now it asks where רבי יוחנן gets his view from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's source is the verse 'והיה כי יביאך... והעברת', which ties the קדושה of בכורות to entering the land. רבי יוחנן says the holiness continued even before that, so he needs his own verse. The בשלמא format means: 'One side is clear, but the other side needs a source.'

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (introduces the side that is already clear)
What is the reason or source?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Reish Lakish,
the reason is as he stated,
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק 'והיה כי יביאך' (שמות 13:11-12).

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yochanan,
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, כִּדְאָמַר טַעַם, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With ריש לקיש's position complete, the גמרא asks for the source of the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי יוחנן's view that the holiness of the בכורות continued after the census.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's answer: 'לי יהיו' means they stay Mine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers with the verse 'לי יהיו' and explains it as 'they will remain in their state.' He adds that seeing רבי יוחנן in a dream showed him his explanation was correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: I saw רבי יוחנן in a dream, which shows that I am saying something good. The verse says 'לי יהיו', 'they shall be Mine', meaning they shall stay as they are.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives רבי יוחנן's source: the words 'לי יהיו' in במדבר 3:13. He reads them as 'they will stay in their holy state.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse already said 'הקדשתי לי כל בכור', 'I sanctified for Me every firstborn.' The extra words 'לי יהיו' are therefore read as a lasting promise: the holiness remains. That directly argues against ריש לקיש's ופסקו. The dream is mentioned as a good sign that רבי אלעזר correctly understood his teacher, רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall remain in their existing state

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's source is 'לי יהיו', which means the בכורות stay holy without any break. ריש לקיש's source is 'והיה כי יביאך', which means the holiness comes back only upon entering the land.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core reading that separates the two אמוראים. One verse is read as permanence, and the other as a fresh start tied to the land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
I saw Rabbi Yochanan in a dream,
[a sign] that I am saying a proper matter:
the verse states: 'Mine they shall be',
[meaning] they shall remain in their state.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲזַאי בְּחֶילְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי יוחנן's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'לי יהיו' teach that the בכורות remain in their holiness, so it never stopped.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן do with ריש לקיש's verse?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוחנן does not use 'והיה כי יביאך' to say the holiness restarts in the land, the גמרא asks what that verse teaches according to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what does he do with the verse 'And it shall be when He brings you... and you shall set apart'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other verse. It asks what רבי יוחנן learns from the verse ריש לקיש used, since the Torah does not write words for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every verse must teach something. If רבי יוחנן holds the holiness never stopped, the verse tying בכורות to entering the land seems to lose its job. This is the classic 'מאי עביד ליה' move: find a different lesson in the verse for the side that does not use it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does that opinion learn from this verse)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan,
'And it shall be when He shall bring you... and you shall set apart',
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, ״וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ... וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing רבי יוחנן's own source, the גמרא asks how he explains ריש לקיש's verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי יוחנן derives from 'והיה כי יביאך... והעברת', since he does not use it to teach that holiness restarts in the land.

steps.title: The verse teaches: this מצוה earns entry into the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses the verse for the teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל: do the מצוה of בכורות, and in its merit you will enter ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that verse for what was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל: Do this מצוה, because in its merit you will enter the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי יוחנן the verse is not about when the holiness begins. It is about a reward: keeping the מצוה of בכורות is what brings you into the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads 'when He brings you into the land' as a time condition, meaning the holiness starts then. רבי יוחנן reads the same link as a cause-and-reward, meaning the מצוה is the reason you will be brought in. So the verse still teaches something, and the מחלוקת stands, with each side's verse fully explained.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
A תנא from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל taught
On account of which, in its merit

steps.whatToRemember: Same verse, two readings. For ריש לקיש, 'כי יביאך' tells you WHEN the holiness returns, upon entering the land. For רבי יוחנן, it tells you WHY you enter the land, as a reward for this מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not denying the verse or the מצוה. He just reads the connection to the land as a reward, not as the starting point of the holiness.

phrases.english: That [verse] is needed by him
for that which the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Perform this מצוה,
on account of which you will enter the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what רבי יוחנן learns from ריש לקיש's verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse teaches that performing the מצוה of בכורות is the merit through which Israel enters the land.

steps.title: רב מרדכי reports a reversed version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי tells רב אשי that his yeshiva teaches the dispute the other way around: רבי יוחנן says the בכורות were not made holy in the מדבר, and ריש לקיש says they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: You teach it this way, but we teach it the opposite way. רבי יוחנן says: the בכורות were not made holy in the מדבר. ריש לקיש says: the בכורות were made holy in the מדבר.
steps.whatsHappening: A different version of the whole dispute from earlier is brought, with the opinions seemingly switched between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, רבי יוחנן held that the holiness of the בכורות in the מדבר never stopped, and ריש לקיש held that it stopped. רב מרדכי's wording seems to flip this. That would turn the whole סוגיא upside down.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi:
You teach it this way,
but we teach it the opposite way:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: the firstborn were not made holy in the wilderness,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר.
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish says: the firstborn were made holy in the wilderness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן הָכִי מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן אִיפְּכָא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a rival version of the base dispute that the sugya has been analyzing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב מרדכי's tradition, רבי יוחנן says 'לא קדשו' and ריש לקיש says 'קדשו'.

steps.title: רב אשי asks whether everything else must also be reversed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges him: if you reverse the opinions, do you also reverse the objections and רבי אלעזר's dream statement?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Do you also reverse the objection? And do you reverse what רבי אלעזר said?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back. He argues that flipping the names would force you to flip the whole discussion built on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוגיא contains objections against each position and רבי אלעזר's statement that his reading of רבי יוחנן was confirmed in a dream. Those only fit the original assignment of opinions. If the names are switched, all of that falls apart, which shows the reversed version is hard to accept.

phrases.english: He (Rav Ashi) said to him:
And do you also reverse the objection,
and do you reverse that statement of Rabbi Elazar?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אלעזר's פסוק 'לי יהיו' and his dream about רבי יוחנן (step 3).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָפְכִית נָמֵי תְּיוּבָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reversed version from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרדכי's reversed version of the dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Switching the opinions would require switching all the objections and רבי אלעזר's dream-confirmed reading, which cannot work.

steps.title: רב מרדכי explains that 'not made holy' means 'did not need to be made holy'
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי answers that in his version, 'לא קדשו' means the בכורות did not need anyone to make them holy, because they were already holy on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'They were not made holy' means 'they did not need to be made holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי shows that his words do not actually flip the opinions. Only the wording is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his version, when רבי יוחנן says 'לא קדשו,' he means no act of making them holy was needed, because their holiness was automatic. That is the same as the standard view that for רבי יוחנן the holiness never stopped. So nothing else in the סוגיא needs to be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: to be made holy (through an act of הקדש)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב מרדכי's version has רבי יוחנן saying the בכורות had no holiness. 'לא קדשו' here means they were already holy without needing anyone to sanctify them.

phrases.english: He (Rav Mordechai) said to him:
'They were not made holy' means:
they did not need to be made holy (they were already holy).

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ לְהוּ — לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לִיקְדַּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מרדכי's version reverses the opinions of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the words differ. 'לא קדשו' means they needed no act of sanctifying, so the opinions themselves stay the same.

steps.title: If so, it is the same as our version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the meaning is identical, רב מרדכי's version is just our version, so why bring it up?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is our version!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רב מרדכי bothered to report his version if it means the same thing. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After step 8, there is no real disagreement between the two versions. So the גמרא wants to know what רב מרדכי gained by presenting a confusing alternate wording.

keyTerms.meaning: that is the same as ours

phrases.english: If so,
that is the same as ours!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דִּידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רב מרדכי's explanation: if the meaning is the same, his version seems pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרדכי's choice to present his alternate version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two versions mean the same thing, reporting a different wording adds nothing.

steps.title: A student must repeat his teacher's exact words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב מרדכי teaches us something: a person must quote his teacher in the teacher's own language.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us: a person must say a teaching in the words of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב מרדכי kept his teacher's wording even though the meaning matched, and this shows a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרדכי could have just said 'we agree.' Instead he kept the exact words he received, 'לא קדשו,' and then explained them. This shows that a tradition must be passed on in the teacher's language, not changed into one's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: a person must say a teaching in his teacher's exact words

steps.whatToRemember: רב מרדכי's version only sounds reversed. Its meaning matches the standard version, and the lesson is that one must quote one's teacher's exact words.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'חייב אדם לומר בלשון רבו' is a basic principle of how תורה שבעל פה is passed down faithfully.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
a person must say it in the language of his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: חַיָּיב אָדָם לוֹמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches the duty to keep one's teacher's exact wording.

steps.title: קונטרוקוס asks where 300 לויים went
steps.stepSummary: קונטרוקוס the officer asks רבן יוחנן בן זכאי why the family-by-family count of the לויים adds up to 22,300, while the tribe's total count is only 22,000.
steps.simpleTranslation: קונטרוקוס the officer asked רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: In the separate counts of the לויים you find 22,300. In their total you find 22,000. Where did the 300 go?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. A Roman officer points out a gap in the numbers of the לויים in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to our topic because the לויים replaced the בכורות in the מדבר, which is how their holiness was cancelled. The family totals in במדבר chapter 3 add up to 22,300, but the summary number is 22,000. The officer wants to know what happened to the extra 300, and the answer comes next.

phrases.english: Kontrokos the officer asked
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai:
In the individual counts of the Levites you find
twenty-two thousand three hundred,

phrases.aramaic: בִּכְלָלָן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁנַיִם אֶלֶף,
phrases.english: but in their total you find twenty-two thousand,
so where did the three hundred go?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל קוּנְטְרוּקוּס הַשַּׂר אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section about the לויים replacing the בכורות in the מדבר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the total count of the לויים is 300 fewer than the sum of the family counts.

steps.title: The extra 300 Levites were firstborns themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains that the 300 extra לויים were בכורות. A בכור cannot cancel the holiness of another בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Those 300 were firstborns, and a firstborn cannot release the holiness of another firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers קונטרוקוס's question from step 11 about the missing 300 לויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The total of 22,000 only counts the לויים who could stand in place of a firstborn ישראל. The 300 extra לויים were firstborns themselves. So they could not take over the holiness of an Israelite firstborn, and the Torah left them out of the total.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels or releases (a holiness or status)

steps.confusionAlert: The 300 לויים really were counted; they are not missing. They are just left out of the 22,000, because that number only counts the לויים who could replace an Israelite firstborn.

phrases.english: He (Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai) said to him:
Those three hundred were firstborns,
and a firstborn cannot release (the holiness of) a firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹתָן שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת בְּכוֹרוֹת הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the 300-person gap asked in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 300 extra לויים were firstborns, and a firstborn cannot redeem another firstborn, so they were not counted in the 22,000.

steps.title: Why can't a firstborn release another firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule that a בכור cannot cancel another בכור's holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to ask why this rule is true. It is setting up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other לוי could take the place of a firstborn ישראל. The גמרא wants to know what makes a firstborn לוי different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind the rule stated in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a firstborn לוי cannot cancel the holiness of a firstborn ישראל.

steps.title: אביי: a firstborn can only cancel his own holiness
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a firstborn לוי's status as a לוי is only enough to cancel his own firstborn holiness, and no one else's.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is enough for a firstborn to release his own holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the reason for the rule from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn לוי carries the holiness of a firstborn himself. His being a לוי is 'used up' freeing his own firstborn holiness. Nothing is left over to free another person's.
steps.whatToRemember: The 22,000 count only includes לויים who could replace a firstborn ישראל. Firstborn לויים were left out, because they only freed themselves.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is enough for the firstborn to release his own holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דַּיּוֹ לַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A firstborn לוי's status only covers his own firstborn holiness, so he cannot free anyone else.

steps.title: The numbers: silver collected versus silver given
steps.stepSummary: קונטרוקוס asks a second question. The Torah's numbers show about 201 talents collected for the משכן, but only 100 talents given.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also asked him: In the collection of silver you find 201 talents and 11 מנה, as it is written: 'A בקע per head, half a שקל by the holy שקל.' But in the giving of the silver you find 100 talents, as it is written: 'And the hundred talents of silver were for casting.'
steps.whatsHappening: קונטרוקוס opens a new question by laying out two numbers that seem not to match. This sets up his accusation against משה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 603,550 men gave half a שקל each, which totals 301,775 שקלים. Counting a talent as 1,500 שקלים (60 מנה of 25 שקלים each), that comes to 201 talents and 11 מנה. Yet the פסוק says only 100 talents were used for casting the sockets.

keyTerms.meaning: Talent, a large unit of weight or money

phrases.english: And he further asked him:
In the collection of silver you find

phrases.aramaic: מָאתַיִם וְאַחַת כִּכָּר וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מָנֶה,
phrases.english: two hundred and one talents and eleven maneh,
as it is written: 'A beka per head,
half a shekel by the holy shekel, etc.'
phrases.notes: Half a shekel for each of 603,550 men = 301,775 shekels.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִנְתִינַת הַכֶּסֶף אַתָּה מוֹצֵא מְאַת כִּכָּר,
phrases.english: but in the giving of the silver you find one hundred talents,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי מְאַת כִּכַּר הַכֶּסֶף לָצֶקֶת וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it is written: 'And the hundred talents of silver were for casting, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד שְׁאָלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second number puzzle from the same questioner after the first was resolved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 201 talents collected matches only 100 talents given.

steps.title: The accusation: was משה a thief, a gambler, or bad at math?
steps.stepSummary: קונטרוקוס uses the gap to accuse משה: he gave half, kept half, and did not even give back a full half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was משה your teacher a thief, or a gambler, or not skilled in accounting? He gave half and took half, and he did not even return a full half!
steps.whatsHappening: קונטרוקוס turns the number gap into a sharp attack on משה רבינו's honesty or skill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He offers three options: stealing, gambling the money away, or a math mistake. The 'not even a full half' jab works because half of about 201 talents is more than 100. So even the half משה supposedly gave seems short.

phrases.english: Was Moses your teacher a thief,
or was he a gambler,
or was he not skilled in accounting?
He gave half and took half,
and he did not even return a complete half.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֹשֶׁה רַבְּכֶם גַּנָּב הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an accusation from the number gap laid out in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The honesty or competence of משה רבינו as treasurer of the משכן funds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: About 201 talents came in and only 100 went out. So משה must have stolen, gambled, or miscalculated, and he gave back less than even half.

steps.title: The holy מנה was double
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers that משה was honest and skilled. The 'holy' מנה used to measure the 100 talents was double the regular מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: משה רבינו was a trustworthy treasurer and was skilled in accounting, but the מנה of the Sanctuary was double.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי defends משה and shows that the two numbers really do match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 100 talents were counted in holy units, where a מנה is 50 שקלים instead of 25. So 100 holy talents equal 200 regular talents. The remaining talent and 11 מנה (1,775 שקלים) were used for the hooks, as the next פסוק (שמות 38:28) says.

keyTerms.meaning: The מנה of the Sanctuary (the holy מנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Both puzzles have the same lesson: the Torah's numbers seem not to match only because the outsider did not know a hidden rule. In the first it was firstborn לויים; in the second it was the double holy מנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the 'holy שקל' in the first פסוק with the 'holy מנה' in this answer. The point here is that the 100 talents were counted in a bigger unit, so they are worth twice as much.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Moses our teacher was a trustworthy treasurer,
and he was skilled in accounting,
but the maneh of the Sanctuary was double.
phrases.notes: A holy מנה was 50 שקלים instead of 25, so 100 holy talents equal 200 regular ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ גִּיזְבָּר נֶאֱמָן הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the accusation of step 16 by fixing the units used in the count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the unit of measure: the holy maneh is double the regular one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 100 talents given were regular talents, so about half the silver went missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 100 talents were holy talents, equal to 200 regular talents. The silver fully matches, and משה was honest and accurate.

steps.title: רב אחאי asks what really bothered קונטרוקוס
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי asks which verse made קונטרוקוס's question work. If it was the verse about casting the sockets, there is an easy answer: those 100 talents were for casting, and the rest went to the treasury.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי discussed it: What was hard for him? Was it the verse 'And the hundred talents of silver were for casting'? These were for casting, and the others went to the treasury!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי questions the basis of קונטרוקוס's attack. He points out that the verse he seems to rely on only says 100 talents were used for casting. It never says that only 100 talents were collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about casting the אדנים (sockets) tells us how much silver was used for one job. It does not tell us the total amount collected. So the 'missing' 101 talents could simply have been stored in the treasury, and קונטרוקוס would have no question at all.

phrases.english: Rav Achai discussed it:
What was difficult for him,
"And the hundred talents of silver were
for casting, etc."?
phrases.notes: שמות 38:27, about casting the sockets of the משכן.

phrases.english: These were for casting,
and those others went to the treasury!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי בַּהּ רַב אַחַאי: מַאי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to examine the basis of קונטרוקוס's question from steps 15 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basis of קונטרוקוס's claim that only 100 talents were given.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The casting verse only reports 100 talents used for one purpose. The remaining silver could have been placed in the treasury, so there is no gap to explain.

steps.title: Another verse says the total collection was 100 talents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a different verse lists the whole amount collected from the people, and it also says only 100 talents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another verse is written: 'And the silver of those counted of the congregation was a hundred talents.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחאי's challenge. קונטרוקוס was relying on a verse that gives the total collected, not just the amount used for casting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse describes all the silver collected from the people who were counted. Since even the total is only 100 talents, there is no room to say that extra silver went to the treasury. So קונטרוקוס's question stands, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer was needed.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
"And the silver of those counted of the congregation
was a hundred talents, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 38:25, about the total amount collected.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַב קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different verse as the true source of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קונטרוקוס seemed to rely only on the casting verse, which leaves room for silver in the treasury.
steps.terutzMaskana: He relied on the verse giving the total collection, which also says 100 talents. So the gap is real.

steps.title: How did he know the holy מנה was double?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רבן יוחנן בן זכאי had for his claim that the holy מנה was double the regular one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what he told him, that the holy מנה was double, where does he know that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer from step 17 and asks for his source. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole answer to קונטרוקוס depends on the holy מנה being double. Without a source, this could look like a convenient excuse. So the גמרא wants a proof from the verses themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: And that which he said to him
The holy מנה (the unit used for the משכן)
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And that which he said to him:
the holy maneh was double,
from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה, מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer in step 17 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the claim that the holy מנה was double the regular מנה.

steps.title: Proposed proof from the 1,775 שקלים
steps.stepSummary: The proof comes from the verse itself. It lists 1,775 שקלים in small coins. With a regular מנה, that adds up to 71 מנה, which is more than a full talent. Then the Torah should have said '101 talents and 11 מנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from the verse itself: here there are 71 מנה, as it says 'And of the 1,775 he made hooks for the pillars.' The verse counted them only in small coins. If the מנה were regular, it should have said 101 talents and 11 מנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a proof from the same passage. It points to the extra 1,775 שקלים and asks why the Torah did not convert them into a larger unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מנה is 25 שקלים, so 1,775 שקלים is 71 מנה. A talent is 60 מנה, so that is one full talent plus 11 מנה. If that were true, the Torah would have said '101 talents and 11 מנה' instead of listing the amount in loose שקלים. The fact that it did not means the amount was less than a talent, which only works if the מנה was larger.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say from it itself (from this same verse)
Small units / loose coins (here, individual שקלים)

steps.confusionAlert: The word אִילֵימָא signals a suggested source that the גמרא will end up rejecting. That is what happens here. The proof is stated in full and concluded in the next step, but in step 23 (וְדִילְמָא) the גמרא rejects it.

phrases.english: If you say from it itself,
for here there are seventy-one maneh
"And of the one thousand seven hundred
and seventy-five
he made hooks for the pillars,"
phrases.notes: שמות 38:28. 1,775 שקלים ÷ 25 שקלים per regular מנה = 71 מנה.

phrases.english: and the verse counted them only in small units,
and if it were so (that the maneh was regular),
one hundred and one talents
and eleven maneh it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא מִינֵּיהּ, שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּאן שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof requested in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That the holy מנה was double the regular מנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 38:28. The 1,775 שקלים are listed in small coins rather than converted into a talent plus מנה.

steps.title: Conclusion: the holy מנה was double
steps.stepSummary: Because the Torah lists the extra silver in loose שקלים, we learn that the holy מנה was double. That makes 1,775 שקלים only 35½ מנה, which is less than a talent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the verse counts them only in small units, learn from it: the holy מנה was double.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion of the proof. The holy מנה was double, which confirms רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a holy מנה of 50 שקלים, 1,775 שקלים is only 35½ מנה. That is not enough for a full talent of 60 מנה, which would explain why the Torah lists it as loose coins. This proof does not hold: the very next step rejects it.
steps.whatToRemember: If the holy מנה is 50 שקלים, then 100 holy talents plus 1,775 שקלים exactly match the full collection. But this particular proof from the 1,775 שקלים is rejected in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first attempt to ground רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer in the verses. It depends on assuming the Torah always converts amounts worth a talent or more into talents. Step 23 challenges exactly that assumption.

phrases.english: Rather, since the verse did not count them
except in small units,
learn from it:
the holy maneh was double.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִדְּלֹא מְנָאָן הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא בִּפְרוֹטְרוֹט, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the proof from step 21 into a final conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Based on the 1,775 שקלים, the holy מנה seems to be double the regular one. This is a tentative conclusion that step 23 rejects.

steps.title: Maybe the Torah counts only the big totals in talents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the silver proof. Maybe the Torah lists only the main hundreds in talents and lists every leftover amount in שקלים, even when the leftover is more than a talent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the verse counts the general (big) amounts in talents, and does not count the details (smaller amounts) in talents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 21-22. It offers another reason why the Torah might have written the extra silver in שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the Torah always turns any amount worth a talent or more into talents. The גמרא suggests a different writing style: the Torah gives the round hundreds (100 talents) in talents and writes all smaller leftover amounts in שקלים. If so, the 1,775 שקלים could equal more than a talent, and nothing proves that the holy מנה was double.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the holy מנה was regular-sized. It is only saying that this verse does not prove it was double.

phrases.english: But perhaps it counts the general amounts in talents,
phrases.notes: The 'general' amount is the round 100 talents.

phrases.english: but does not count the details in talents!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא כְּלָלֵי קָחָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof and conclusion of steps 21-22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the 1,775 שקלים of silver.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the Torah would turn any amount worth a talent into talents. The Torah may instead list only the round totals in talents and all leftovers in שקלים.

steps.title: A new proof from the copper offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof. The copper was 70 talents and 2,400 שקלים. With a regular מנה, 2,400 שקלים equals 96 מנה, which is more than a talent. Yet the Torah still lists it in loose שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from here: 'And the copper of the offering was seventy talents and 2,400 שקלים.' Here there are 96 מנה, and yet the verse counts them only in small units.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second verse to prove the holy מנה was double. This time it uses the copper of the משכן, where the main amount is not a round hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the main amount is 70 talents, not 100, so the 'round hundreds' answer from step 23 does not obviously apply. With a regular מנה of 25 שקלים, 2,400 שקלים is 96 מנה. That is more than a full talent (60 מנה), so the Torah should have written '71 talents and 36 מנה'. Since it did not, the leftover must really be less than a talent.

keyTerms.meaning: The copper that was offered for the משכן
A weight unit; 60 of them make a talent
In small change, in loose small units

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And the copper of the offering was seventy talents
and two thousand four hundred shekels,"
for here there are ninety-six maneh,
phrases.notes: 2,400 ÷ 25 = 96 regular מנה, which is more than one talent of 60 מנה.

phrases.english: and the verse counts them only in small units,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that step 23 rejected with a new verse.
steps.raayaObject: That the holy מנה was double the regular מנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות לח:כט: 70 talents and 2,400 שקלים of copper.

steps.title: So the holy מנה was double
steps.stepSummary: From the copper verse, the גמרא concludes that the holy מנה was double. With a double מנה (50 שקלים), 2,400 שקלים is only 48 מנה, which is less than a talent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: the holy מנה was double.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion of the copper proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a holy מנה is 50 שקלים, then 2,400 שקלים is only 48 מנה. That is less than a talent, so the Torah correctly left it in שקלים. This conclusion will be challenged in the next step.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
the maneh of the Sanctuary was double.
phrases.notes: 50 שקלים instead of 25, so 2,400 שקלים = 48 מנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the proof begun in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The copper verse seems to show that the holy מנה was double.

steps.title: Maybe the Torah counts only the tens in talents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the copper proof too. Maybe the Torah lists only the large unit (the tens of talents) in talents, and writes anything below ten talents in שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it counts a large unit in talents and does not count a small unit in talents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the copper proof with the same kind of argument it used in step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said the Torah might count only round hundreds in talents. Now the גמרא widens the idea: maybe the Torah counts only round tens (like 70) in talents and leaves anything under ten talents in שקלים. If so, 96 regular מנה could still be written in שקלים, and the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A small unit (less than ten talents)

phrases.aramaic: וְדִילְמָא פְּרָטָא רַבָּה קָא חָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי,
phrases.english: But perhaps it counts a large unit in talents,
but does not count a small unit in talents!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא פְּרָטָא רַבָּה קָא חָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the copper proof of steps 24-25 the same way step 23 rejected the silver proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the 2,400 שקלים of copper.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah may write only the round tens in talents and leave any leftover under ten talents in שקלים, so the leftover could still be more than one talent.

steps.title: רב חסדא proves it from יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a verse in יחזקאל that states the size of the holy מנה directly: 20 + 25 + 15 שקלים, a total of 60 שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: the proof is from here: 'And the שקל shall be twenty גרה; twenty שקלים, twenty-five שקלים, ten and five שקלים shall be your מנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since both counting proofs were pushed aside, רב חסדא turns to a verse that openly tells us how big the holy מנה is. The גמרא will work out the math next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proof does not depend on guessing how the Torah chooses to write amounts. The verse itself defines the מנה: 20 + 25 + 10 + 5 = 60 שקלים. This is not simply the 50-שקל double מנה of the earlier steps; the גמרא goes on to explain how this number fits with a holy מנה that was double.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin unit; 20 make a holy שקל
The holy coin, worth a סלע

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs from the numbers in the Torah were rejected because the Torah might list leftovers in שקלים for style reasons. רב חסדא instead uses a verse in יחזקאל that defines the מנה as 60 שקלים; the גמרא goes on to explain how this fits with a holy מנה that was double.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern: when a proof from how a verse is worded can be explained another way, the גמרא looks for a verse that states the rule directly.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said: from here,
"And the shekel shall be twenty gera;
twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels,
ten and five shekels
shall be your maneh."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected copper proof with a direct verse.
steps.raayaObject: That the holy מנה was larger than the regular מנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל מה:יב, which defines the מנה as 20 + 25 + 15 = 60 שקלים.
